COST BASIS: overnight. Specific investment cost for a large greenfield chemical pulp mill. p.1: 'A large-scale chemical pulp mill with an annual pulp production of around 1.4 million tons has an investment cost of about 2.5 billion USD if built from the ground up. The specific investment costs are around 1500-2000 USD/(ton/year).' Table 4 gives the same thing as a scale function: total investment = 1.85 * Capacity^0.6 billion USD with capacity in Mt/yr, of which 0.61 * Capacity^0.6 is the power generation and chemical recovery area - about a third of the capital cost, and the largest single block in a pulp mill (p.7). At 1.4 Mt/yr that function gives 2.27 billion USD, or 1620 USD/(t/yr), against the body's 'about 2.5 billion'; both sit inside the 1500-2000 range. The scale exponent for the industry is 0.6-0.7 (p.7). Cost differences between sites are driven by whether hard or soft wood is used. NO CURRENCY YEAR IS GIVEN ANYWHERE IN THE BRIEF. It says 'USD' and nothing more; the underlying study is EBRD & POYRY 2012, so 2012_USD is the likely basis but the brief does not say so. The brief itself gives no year. 2012_USD assigned from that underlying study by Brad, 2026-09-10 - an assumption made here, not something the brief says.
